gaps: Abide's actual acquisition/marketing tactics could not be found (only competitive-positioning/pricing info via faith.tools); its scale suggests organic/word-of-mouth longevity but no primary source confirms specific channels.

Internal docs disagree on FellowScript's pricing structure: docs/index.md and docs/design/home-page.md describe a 3-tier Free/Individual-$4.99/Group-$9.99 model, while docs/design/account.md (the more implementation-detailed doc) describes a single Group-only tier (1-8 members, priced by member count, no separate Individual plan). This is a documentation inconsistency, not a sourcing gap, but it should be resolved or explicitly caveated before the findings/report stage draws monetization-dependent conclusions (e.g. which growth channels are 'cost-effective' depends on whether solo users have a standalone paid path).

No source was found specifically on Google Play ASO for religious/lifestyle apps (Play Store console mechanics differ from Apple's); gathered ASO sources are either platform-general or Apple-specific. Noted as a minor gap since FellowScript is web+iOS only today (no Android client per docs), so this may be moot.
agent-browser and notebooklm-research skills were not invoked this round — all needed sources were reachable via WebSearch/WebFetch, so their setup status is untested, not confirmed absent.
summary: Read all required internal FellowScript docs (README, docs/index.md, docs/design/{overview,home-page,community,account,notes,bible-reader}.md, docs/architecture/overview.md, mkdocs.yml) to ground the plan in the app's actual mission, features, group-centric social model, monetization, and parchment-and-gold reverent-editorial brand identity — no credential/secret files were opened. Ran two rounds of external web research (WebSearch + WebFetch) covering all five plan-required channel categories: (1) ASO fundamentals via 7 independent guides (Udonis, AppRadar, ASOmobile, Semrush, quokkalabs, dogtownmedia, applyzer); (2) faith-app-specific community/partnership channels via primary and independent sources on Hallow's parish/diocese/university partnerships and TikTok UGC strategy (Branch.io case study, Hallow's own blog, Phiture case study, Contrary Research, Consumer Startups, St. John's press release) and YouVersion's church-partnership tooling and verse-sharing virality (growthcasestudies.com, LinkedIn analysis, ChurchTechToday); (3) competitive landscape for Glorify (techstartups.com + religionnews.com corroborating the same $40M raise) and Abide (faith.tools); (4) content/creator marketing via FrontGate Media (2 pieces) and Christian Post Advertising; (5) referral/virality mechanics generally (7 independent sources: Molfar, Adapty, Reteno, Tapp, ReferralRock) tied specifically to FellowScript's group/seat-based subscription model; (6) campus-ministry and small-group channels (EveryCampus, TheGospelCoalition, ReliantCreative, Caylor Solutions, faith.tools, TheLeadPastor, SmartGroups); (7) indie/small-team marketing capacity-matching (Octospark, IndieHackers, ApsteQ). Every major claim has 2+ independent corroborating sources except the isolated Abide-tactics gap and the single-instance St. John's/Hallow institutional deal, both noted above. Coverage meets the plan's success criteria (3-5+ sources per channel category, all tied to specific FellowScript features/brand elements).
